correctness.rationale: The minimal subtree on the four marked leaves, with degree-two vertices suppressed, has a central edge. An original tree edge inducing that split has two parameters on each side and binary cut rank at most one. Restricted rows or columns have at most two possible patterns on the opposite pair (zero and at most one nonzero pattern), even when the realizing vertex is a parameter. This confines the traces to at most two rows and two columns of the four-by-four table, giving at most 12. Shattering any larger set would shatter each of its quadruples. A fresh exact check verified connectedness and distance-hereditary reduction certificates for both witnesses, the twelve listed four-set traces, and the eight different triple traces. In the 13-vertex witness three traces already occur among the parameters, and each of the other nine vertices realizes a different additional trace. Induced subgraphs retaining the parameters retain exactly their selected profiles, so all 3–12 occur; four isolated vertices and the four-vertex star give 1 and 2. The eight-vertex connected witness shatters three, and no smaller witness can realize eight traces. The replay script is branches/fec4ef40-fb63-42da-b771-ef60cc56fd99/independent_check.py, with CHECK_OK in the completed run. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed. The finite witness checks do not establish the universal bound, which follows from the cut argument.

evidence: Bousquet–Thomassé Lemma 5 gives at most 2^k cross-neighborhood classes at a binary rank-k cut. Theorem 7 bounds distance-2 VC-dimension by 3·2^{k+1}+2, not the four-site all-vertex trace statistic.
The later monadically dependent graph results give polynomial or almost-linear neighborhood complexity bounds in broader settings, not this exact fixed-size maximum and its attainment.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The rank-one cut restriction plus the central edge gives the stated upper bound, but the restricted cross-cut patterns alone do not force the existence of compatible within-side traces. Sharpness and the spectrum need additional graph constructions.

evidence: Even an exact VC dimension of three would give only an upper bound of 15 traces on four sites by Sauer–Shelah. The source actually gives 12 and certifies attainability of each number. The strongest matched subclass results can overlap the triple shattering or lower profile counts but cannot furnish the 12 extremizer.
The distance-hereditary enumeration paper arXiv:1608.01464 counts graphs, not exact distinct adjacency traces on a fixed parameter set.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The general rank-cut lemma provides the numerical obstruction after the two-by-two marked-leaf split, but it does not make every allowed cell jointly realizable. The certified extremizer and its induced-subgraph traces fill that gap. The immediate minimal-order argument for the triple is supportive, not the basis for originality.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Changing the name of the graph class or using the row-trace formulation gives the same test. External-only, closed-neighborhood, equality-sensitive, and WL variants are not interchangeable with it.

residual_risks: These targeted comparisons do not rule out an unindexed exact open-neighborhood formula or separate earlier extremizer. value.rationale: This gives the first parameter size past the class's shattering threshold, where a mere VC bound misses three cells. The rank-one cut explains the sharp obstruction, and the certified graph construction shows its full strength can be attained simultaneously while also determining the intervening cardinalities. This is a useful exact benchmark for adjacency types in distance-hereditary graphs, not just a count from a finite graph list.
